course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
title: Safe Mode: identify the boundary before trusting code
goal: Explain safe-mode and extension-admission boundaries without running unknown code on the host.

prerequisites.text: Complete P1–P9. Distinguish a common-module function from its application caller; preserve your source and run a separate training infobase.

sections.title: The question we are checking
paragraphs: An author says an unknown extension is safe because one checkbox is enabled. Does it restrict user actions, platform capabilities or the whole OS process? Separate those questions without executing third-party code.
Use a new training copy and invented records only. Predict first, then compare the observation; preserve existing functions, files, and records.

sections.title: Practice without executing a file
paragraphs: Complete this task using a fictional text card. Install no extension, change no role, enable no privilege and test no real file/network access. H 1/H 2 are fictional labels for different bytes.

sections.title: Mechanisms solve different problems
paragraphs: Rights constrain user operations, safe mode specific code capabilities, server profiles additional server resources, andVMsan environment boundary. They are not interchangeable. A directive or checkbox does not prove host-file protection against arbitrary configuration modules. Define threat and supported context first.

Separate application roles, platform safe mode and OS isolation. Each controls a different boundary; none alone proves an arbitrary file safe. The beginner route remains ordinary installed official training 1C.

sections.title: A card instead of an executable file
paragraphs: Read the evidence. What is missing for a reasoned admission? A filename and SHA label do not replace source code.

sections.title: Reasoning about the NOT RUN decision
paragraphs: Fictional unknown.cfe card: unknown provenance, no source, arbitrary network and privileged execution requested. Enabled Safe Mode does not supply the missing evidence. Decide NOT RUN before any execution.
The result below is a card-review decision, not program output. No unknown code was executed.

tables.caption: Reasoning about the worked observation
rows: Platform behaviour — Not the whole OS.

sections.title: String execution increases risk
paragraphs: Execute/Evalon user input turns data into a program. Prefer a constrained operation language with explicit validation. Where dynamic execution is required under an official contract, safe mode also needs callable-function restrictions. Do not proposeevalas a universal adapter forStudio code inside a trusted configuration.

Review own extension/processor source and dependencies for dynamic execution, file/network effects, privilege, external components and metadata changes. A keyword alone is not proof of a vulnerability; document required effects and justified admission/refusal.

sections.title: Your prediction first
paragraphs: Is a Safe Mode flag sufficient to admit an unknown extension without source?
Identify the changed action and what should remain unchanged. Reveal the explanation after making your own prediction.

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. Roles, platform restrictions and process isolation solve different problems. Admission needs the exact set, provenance, reviewed source and required permissions. Refusing execution is the correct result here, not failure.

sections.title: Extensions have provenance
paragraphs: Bind an original teaching extension to a base configuration, version and hash. Check borrowed objects, changed methods and preservation after disabling. Compatibility with one version does not cover all upgrades. Exclude proprietary solutions and never execute unknown files merely to obtain PASS.

Use no malicious sample. A fictional card with unknown origin, arbitrary host/privilege requirements and no source must yield NOT RUN. Pure own calculations use minimal inputs and validated ranges rather than global privilege.

sections.title: Trace the boundary decision
paragraphs: This is an admission-decision diagram, not an isolation test. An actual Safe Mode experiment needs an exact version, own reviewed code, an authorised environment and a specific expected refusal. Such execution remains NOT RUN here.

sections.title: An error that can look successful
paragraphs: The bytes match but a dependency changed; or an infobase copy is treated as isolating the entire computer. A hash establishes identity and a copy separates data; neither establishes the claimed OS boundary.
Keep the faulty copy separate. To establish a fix, compare the relevant observation with your prior expectation; do not change an expectation merely to obtain a match.

sections.title: Negative tests must be safe
paragraphs: Use synthetic canaries and a disposable permitted environment without real secrets. Test prohibited files, network, process creation and output limits under the chosen model. Untested boundaries remainPLANNED/NOTRUN. Source hashes prove unchanged bytes, not a complete threat model or protected learner grading.

Actual safe-mode testing needs the exact version, licensed environment, reviewed own code and a specified allowed operation/rejection. Until run it remains PLANNED. Remove untested protection promises from instructions and acceptance records.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: New card: an own extension has reviewed source H 1, but offered build H 2 adds an unreviewed dependency. Make a three-row table: role, Safe Mode, OS isolation—what each may restrict and what is untested here. Give two NOT RUN reasons and a safe next step. Install or execute nothing.
Reveal the reference after recording your own table and decision.

sections.title: Where to complete this task
paragraphs: Record your boundary table and NOT RUN reasons in the self-check explanation; explicitly report no execution in the self-report. Compare the reference after your attempt.

sections.title: Limits of the observation and your explanation
paragraphs: Only the described training actions are established. Two concurrent sessions, clusters, field latency, debugger GUI and arbitrary external-code safety remain separate. Execution, a saved mark and learner understanding are distinct.
State the evidence required before admission and why a single flag cannot replace it.

selfcheck.prompt: Is a Safe Mode flag sufficient to admit an unknown extension without source?
options: No: provenance and boundaries are unestablished
Yes: it protects the entire OS
selfcheck.feedback: No. Roles, platform restrictions and process isolation solve different problems. Admission needs the exact set, provenance, reviewed source and required permissions. Refusing execution is the correct result here, not failure.
They have different boundaries and capabilities.

selfcheck.prompt: Does a file-infobase copy establish complete isolation of host files?
options: No: the process retains its OS permissions
Yes: the infobase path protects all files
selfcheck.feedback: State the evidence required before admission and why a single flag cannot replace it.

selfcheck.prompt: For the new card,explain two refusal reasons,the three mechanism boundaries and a safe next step.
selfcheck.feedback: The answer is not graded automatically. Compare the reasoning with concrete observations from your work.

referenceSolution.source:
Decision: NOT RUN.
Reason 1: buildH 2 differs from reviewedH 1.
Reason 2: a new dependency is unreviewed.
Role: application actions; review the complete role set.
Safe Mode: supported platform restrictions; not actually tested here.
OS isolation: process/environment permissions; an infobase copy does not establish it.
Next: obtain the exact source/dependency set and review without execution.
